comment: Still no lossless in Premium and now they want more money for the same thing. Tidal and Deezer already include hi-fi and Apple Music does too. If they're raising the price they should at least add lossless. I'm pretty much on Tidal full time at this point.

So they want MORE money for a home screen that is TikTok inspired junk. Bring back the old UI or I'm done. Recently played and my playlists are gone and I'm not paying for scrolling cards. Apple Music is looking real good right now.

Another price hike for an app that gets worse with every redesign. Recommendations are stale, shuffle and autoplay are a mess, and the home page is still confusing. I stay for the playlists and podcasts but YouTube Music is looking better every month.

Cool, pay more for a playlist app that still can't show me my liked songs inside a playlist and can't add duplicates on mobile. Enhance keeps shoving recommended tracks into my stuff. I already left Premium over this crap, so the price doesn't change anything for me, but it's still annoying.

A dollar more for no ads, offline downloads and casting is still a no-brainer. The free tier is basically unusable so I'm not going anywhere. My actual complaint is the promoted stuff and pop-ups that show up even for Premium users, but the price itself is fine.

A dollar more is nothing for the whole catalog. Still an incredible deal, honestly it should cost more if it means artists get paid better. Tidal's payout plan is not really in place yet so there's no real alternative for the artists side. Pay the artists, that's the moral case.

Ugh. Another dollar on top when I already can't pay consistently some months. Probably dropping back to the free experience for a while. And of course I'll get the renew emails after cancelling, great.

Apple Music is a way better deal. Lossless and Spatial Audio are included in the same plan, and Spotify is cheap in my country but the sound quality is still lossy. I like Spotify Connect and Chromecast but I prefer Apple Music now and this hike makes the choice easier.

Pay more for the same app that keeps changing under me? I already have auto updates off and an old version installed so I don't have to deal with the new layout. If they force the new layout permanently I'm out, and I already cancelled once after an update I didn't want.

Price going up while they keep taking features away with no explanation. Half the time the features roll out to some users only and then disappear again. I would pay a one-time price for an app that does what this one used to do, so the monthly hike is a hard sell.

Paying more and I still get ads in my podcasts. Premium is supposed to be ad-free but that clearly isn't the case for podcasts, and they keep pushing shows on me. If they keep this up I'm looking at YouTube Premium. Just want music.

I already cancelled my family plan over the podcast-stuffed home screen. A price hike doesn't change anything for me. The home page is still full of shows I never play and I can't permanently hide them. Show me the music.

Eh, I'm on free and fine with ads as long as I can hear what I like. Premium is still worth it if you want to pick songs and skip without ads, but $11 is a bit much when the free tier mostly does the job for me. I'll probably end up paying again eventually.

Honestly a dollar more is fine, the library is still the best and I keep coming back after trying others. My gripe is the recs that keep suggesting songs I already have and personalized playlists repeating the same picks. Hopefully some of the money goes into better recommendations.
Family plan going up a dollar is nothing when you split it between the household. A few bucks each a month and every person still gets their own account and no ads. Still worth every penny for us.

Not paying anything since I cancelled, but the renew subscription pop-up still shows up every time I open the app. Clearing cache and reinstalling did nothing. Anyone else getting this after the last update? It's annoying as hell.

Absolutely hate this update. The music tab is a feed of cards now and autoplay keeps playing songs I didn't pick. I cancelled premium over this layout, and I'm switching to Apple Music if the new music tab stays. Price hike is just salt in the wound. No way to contact support either.

Basic stuff like the heart button should not be behind a paywall and now they want more money. Liked songs are mixed into playlist updates, I can't see liked tracks inside playlists, and video clips autoplay while I browse. I'm switching back to Apple Music if this doesn't get fixed, I might unsubscribe.

Per-stream royalties are already fractions of a cent and now they charge more for the same thing. Spotify does not pay artists more than the others, and the scarcity game with label deals is not helping musicians. I'm staying out of habit but this doesn't sit right with me.

Premium is still a good bang for the buck for the huge catalog and the lifestyle features. Around $11 a month just to kill ads is a bit much for me though, and I keep an eye on how the free tier is getting more ads. I'm fine paying it for now and can leave whenever quality drops.

Shuffle is still not random and it plays the same songs from my big playlists again and again. Now it takes two taps to reach regular shuffle. I pay for Spotify mostly for the UI and Connect but if shuffle doesn't get fixed I'm seriously looking at Apple Music, and the price bump makes it worse.

Price doesn't bother me much. I'm here for the algorithm and the catalog, and no other service matches the features yet. Spotify hides play counts and the radio keeps filling with songs I already know, which is the real issue, but I'm not leaving over a dollar.

Spotify still has no lossless tier and now they're charging more. Tidal and Qobuz already offer hi-fi for similar or less money, and artists get paid better there. I'll keep Spotify for Connect and discovery but the sound is still the reason I'm on Tidal. Spotify HiFi would be worth paying extra for, just give it to us.

Oh no, the student price going up. It was already a great deal with Hulu and Showtime included, but I'm on a tight student budget. If the student plan goes up I'm honestly going back to Apple Music, which is what I said I'd do. Anyone else get charged twice for the student discount?

Another price increase and the app still breaks after every update. Reinstalling is the only thing that fixes playback half the time, and my downloads still won't play offline. Turn off auto update and wait for a fix. Customer service is slow or nonexistent.

Not paying more for an app that still can't show me my liked songs on albums and artist pages. I already unsubscribed once, and if they keep taking features away I will unsubscribe again. Daily mix is nice but it's not worth the money with this track list.

A dollar more a month and not one word about what artists get from it. Per-stream royalties are fractions of a cent and this does nothing for them. I'm still here out of habit, but this is exactly the kind of thing that makes me look at where my money actually goes.

Timing is interesting. They raise Premium while still testing stuff and quietly pulling features. I'm hoping the bump comes with features coming back, but I doubt it. If the ones I actually use don't return, I'll vote with my wallet.

Honestly the price going up doesn't change much for me, I'm on an older app version anyway. If they force the new layout on everyone permanently that's a different story, and I'd cancel over that before I cared about a buck.

A dollar isn't what bugs me. Spotify still hides exact play counts and manual album radio is gone, which is what I actually want. Nothing else matches the catalog and building playlists with friends though, so I'm not leaving. Anyone found a good stats.fm workaround for play counts?

Spotify is raising prices and still has no lossless, while Apple Music already gives you lossless and Spatial Audio in the same plan. I like the Chromecast and Android Auto support here, but I'm honestly close to switching back to Apple Music.

Still worth it. Premium gives me more value than all my other subscriptions combined, no ads and offline downloads are what I pay for. A dollar is nothing, and the free tier is basically unusable anyway.

Price goes up and the app still breaks after every update. I reinstalled twice this month and my downloaded songs still won't play offline. Maybe the extra dollar goes toward fixing bugs, we'll see. Support has not gotten back to me.

I cancelled months ago and the renew subscription pop-up still shows up every time I open the app. Now they're raising prices too, great. Clearing cache and reinstalling did nothing, so does anyone have an actual fix?

I'd pay the extra buck if shuffle actually worked. It still plays like twenty songs out of my 800-song playlist, and smart shuffle keeps stuffing recommendations into my playlists. Apple Music's shuffle looks better every week.
Honestly this was overdue. $10 for the whole catalog is still a steal, and artists are getting pennies per stream, so I'd rather see Spotify spend more on them. Still a good deal for what you get.

I'm on free and fine with the ads for now, so the price bump doesn't hit me much. I keep getting tempted to pay again just to skip songs and kill the ads, but random-only shuffle on free is the real annoyance.

A dollar more is fine for me. It's still good bang for the buck for the catalog and no ads, though ten bucks just to remove ads is a lot. I care more about how the free tier's ads are changing than this bump.

Ugh, the student plan going from $4.99 to $5.99 is a big jump when you're on a student budget. I said I'd go back to Apple Music if this happened, and I'm kind of going to. The Hulu bundle is still great but it's getting harder to justify.

Paying more for Spotify and still no lossless. Tidal all the way, they already do hi-fi for similar money. Playlists and discovery are good, but that isn't enough for me to pay more for compressed audio.

Raising the price while my liked songs still don't show up on album pages? Not worth the money right now. I've unsubscribed before and I will again if they keep taking features away. Daily Mix is the only reason I'm still here.

Spotify is raising prices and still has no lossless, while other services have it at similar or lower prices. I keep Spotify for Connect and recommendations, but I'm mostly on Tidal already and this makes it easy to drop Spotify. Artists also get paid less here than on Tidal.
The price bump is a fair bit, but the library and Discover Weekly are still why I'm here. Recommendations repeating songs I already know is my real gripe. I'm not switching over a dollar or so.

I can't keep up with this. Premium was already hard some months and now it's another dollar. I'll probably cancel and go back to the free version and deal with the shuffle. Please don't make me get the renewal pop-up again after I cancel.

Absolutely hate this update. The music tab is a pile of feed cards now and shuffle needs extra taps. Now they're raising the price too. I'm considering canceling my premium and switching to Apple Music if this layout stays.

We cancelled our family plan over the podcast-stuffed home screen and now they're raising prices on top of it. Show me the music, I can't permanently hide podcasts. Not paying more for an app that keeps shoving podcasts in my face.
Price going up on a family plan while the home screen is TikTok-style junk? This is garbage. Bring back the old UI or I'm considering canceling my subscription, I'm done paying for stuff I can't use.
The family plan going up a dollar works out to a few cents more per person in our house, and it's still worth it for no ads. Separate accounts are the main reason we stay, so it's fine by me.

Premium going up while enhance keeps adding stuff to my playlists and I can't see liked songs inside a playlist. I already left once over sorting. If they take away one more thing I'm done, and the price bump is just the cherry on top.
I pay for Premium and ads still play in podcasts. Now the price goes up and they keep pushing podcasts onto my home screen. I just want music, so I'm watching YouTube Premium and Overcast closely.

Premium going up while the heart button is gone on mobile and liked songs are dumped into my playlist updates?? I AM NOT PAYING MORE FOR THIS. I might unsubscribe. Adding a song to several playlists at once is the only thing keeping me here.

The UI is a mess and the recommendations are getting stale, and now they want more money for it? Podcasts and music in one app is still useful, but if the next redesign is as bad as the last one I'm going to look at YouTube Music.
ugh so Premium is $10.99 now and I can barely swing $9.99 some months. I'll probably just drop back to free again until I get paid. The no ads and unlimited skips are what I miss though.
Still think Premium is the best deal going. Ad free, offline downloads, casting, all for a dollar more. The free tier is basically unusable so I'm not really worried about it.

Another increase and still no lossless. Apple Music and Tidal already do hi-fi at this price or less, so Spotify is asking more for a worse product. I already moved my listening to Tidal for this exact reason.
$1 more a month for the SAME garbage TikTok home screen?? I'm DONE. Bring back the old UI or I'm canceling my family plan and going to Apple Music, this is garbage.

Ten-ish dollars for an ad-free catalog is still good value for me, I just think it's getting harder to justify when the free tier keeps getting more ads. Price bump is fine, not thrilled. I'll stay for the lifestyle features.
Cool, price goes up and I'm still stuck with a layout I didn't ask for. I already cancelled after the last forced update and reverted to an old version. Don't upgrade, keep auto updates off.
More money for a Spotify that still won't show my liked songs on album track lists? Not worth it. If they keep taking features away I'm going to unsubscribe again. Pandora has been looking better.

PRICE GOES UP AND THEY STILL WON'T FIX THE HEART BUTTON OR THE PLAYLIST SHARING. I'll pay an add-on for the heart button, I'm serious. Might unsubscribe and go back to Apple Music if this keeps going.
Price hike with the app still crashing after the last update? I reinstalled, I rolled back, the downloads still won't play offline. I'll wait and see but I'm not impressed.

Curious how the new prices shake out for the family and duo plans. Personally the radio and algorithm are still the best thing about it, but I'd love play counts back. stats.fm still does the heavy lifting for me.

Absolutely hate this update. They jacked the price and the music tab is STILL a feed of cards. I'm considering canceling my premium and switching to Apple Music, no way to contact anyone to complain either.

Spotify is raising the price on a plan that still has no lossless and pays artists less than Tidal. I keep Spotify for Connect and recs, but it's getting harder to justify. Would pay more for HiFi, they just won't offer it.

Honestly the free version is fine as long as the ads are tolerable, so I'm not going to rush. But a random shuffle and no skips on free is still annoying, and I keep being tempted to just pay. Eh, we'll see.

Price going up when they still can't show liked songs inside a playlist and the enhance feature keeps sneaking songs in. I already left Premium over that once. One more missing feature and I'm ending my subscription for good.

Student plan is still at $5.99 which is ok, but it went up a dollar so I'm watching it. Hulu is still included which keeps me happy. If the student price keeps going up I'd probably go back to Apple Music, but for now it's worth it.

Apple Music gets you lossless and Spatial Audio in the same plan, so the price hike on Spotify makes it even harder to justify. Spotify is still cheap but I keep feeling like I get less. Prefer Apple Music, and I'd switch for the sound quality alone.
Every time I open the app the renewal pop-up shows up even though I cancelled. Clearing cache and reinstalling didn't help. Anyone else? Annoying window keeps popping up after updates.

So Premium costs more now and I still get ads in podcasts. The whole point of paying is ad free, and I just want music. If podcast ads keep playing I'm going to YouTube Premium, I'm done paying for this.
Price hike? I already cancelled my family plan because the home screen is bombarded with podcasts and I can't permanently hide them. Show me the music, not another podcast. Gone.

Price is going up and they still haven't brought back the features they quietly removed. Some of these are only rolling out to a few users. Vote with your wallet if you care, I'm watching the beta posts.
Family plan going from $15.99 to $16.99 is about a dollar more split across the house, so it's still worth every penny to us. Separate accounts and no ads, we'd never go back to free.

Price hike and shuffle still isn't random. It keeps hitting the same handful of songs from my big playlists. Smart shuffle is adding recommended stuff into my playlists too. Apple Music is looking better every time I open this.

The UI keeps getting worse with every redesign and the recs are stale. I still use it for the podcasts and playlists, but if this keeps going I'm moving to YouTube Music. Price bump is the least of my problems.
Honestly $10.99 for the whole catalog is still a steal, and I'd argue it should be higher given what artists actually get. Pay the artists, this is a moral case. Good to see the price moving.

Price goes up and artists still get fractions of a cent per stream. Spotify is raising prices while royalty rates stay the same, that's the real story. I keep it out of habit but I know other services pay more per stream.
Price bump is fine, honestly still cheap for the library. Discover Weekly keeps suggesting songs I already have though, so I'd love more variety. Still sticking around for the discovery.

A dollar isn't going to make me leave, honestly. My real gripe is that Discover Weekly and song radio keep handing me stuff already sitting in my library. Fix the recs and I'll happily pay the extra buck.

Honestly the full catalog for eleven bucks is still a steal, and if it means artists get paid a bit more per stream I'm all for it. Tidal can talk about artist payouts all it wants, but I'm staying put for now.

Price goes up a buck and the per-stream royalty still rounds to fractions of a cent for the artist. Spotify is raising prices while artists are still getting crumbs, so the money is not going where people think it is.

Apple Music is already lossless with Spatial Audio for basically the same money, and now Spotify wants more for the same thing without better sound. I think this is the nudge I needed to go back to Apple Music, the desktop app and Connect aren't worth much more.

Cool, more money for shuffle that still isn't random!!! I can't even get a true shuffle through my own playlists without the algorithm stepping in. Price hike means nothing when the basics are broken.

Great, they're charging more for a product that still won't let me see liked songs inside a playlist or add duplicates on mobile. I already left once over playlist stuff, so if they keep dropping the things I actually use, I'm done paying.

A buck more is annoying but Premium still does a lot for the money, so I'm not bolting over it. My bigger worry is the free tier getting more ads, because that's what makes the paid plan worth it in the first place.
Family plan going to $16.99 is still a few bucks per person for us, which beats paying for ads. We're keeping it, though I wish the duo and family setup weren't so confusing to switch into.

I already cancelled my family plan over the podcast-stuffed home screen, so this price bump just confirms I'm not paying for a service that keeps shoving shows at me. Show me the music, not another price increase.
Student plan going from $4.99 to $5.99 hurts, and I literally said I'd go back to Apple Music if this happened. Hulu is still included, but I'm on a tight budget so I'm switching back.

Price going up when the UI keeps getting worse every redesign is a tough sell. Recommendations are still stale and the home page is a mess, so I'm watching this closely and YouTube Music is looking better every update.
Another price increase and still no lossless. Tidal and Deezer already give hi-fi at similar prices, so Spotify is asking for more while the sound stays the same. I'm moving to Tidal full time.
Price going up is fine on paper but I'd rather they fix the bugs first. Every update I'm reinstalling, rolling back, and waiting on support, and downloads still won't play offline.
I'm not even paying anymore, but the renew subscription pop-up is still hitting me every time I open the app. Reinstalled, cleared cache, nothing. Anyone know how to get rid of this thing?

Still worth it. Ad-free, offline downloads and casting for a price rise of a dollar is fine with me, and it's still way better value than the free tier. The app itself is my real complaint but I'm not canceling over this.
Paying more so I can still get ads in podcasts and get shoved more shows? No thanks. If they keep pushing podcasts and ads keep playing on Premium, I'm going to YouTube Premium.
Absolutely hate this update, and now they want more money for it. If the new music tab layout stays I'm switching to Apple Music, I'm done with the extra taps and the autoplay nonsense.

Price going up while the features I want are still gone. Probably rolling out slowly to some users, I'd bet this is about the UI sticking. Vote with your wallet, people, and vote in those feature requests too.

A price increase on the family plan while they keep the TikTok-style home screen? This is garbage. I'm considering canceling my subscription and moving to Apple Music or Tidal, I'm done paying for this junk.
Can't afford it some months as it is, so an extra dollar is just making it harder. I'll probably cancel the plan and go back to the free version, and I'm sick of the renew prompts after I cancel too.
Price going up doesn't change much for me since I'm running an older version anyway. If they force the new layout through a update I'll cancel again, same as last time.

A price increase doesn't do much for me since I'm still on free, though I was kind of tempted to resubscribe. Free is fine as long as the ads are tolerable, and skipping songs on Premium is still what I'd pay for.
Cool, they raise the price and still no liked songs on album track lists. If they keep taking features away I'll unsubscribe again, because right now this isn't worth money.

Paying more for a service where I can't see my liked songs in playlists, can't share playlists, and get autoplay video ads while I browse? I'm switching back to Apple Music, and I might just unsubscribe for good.

A dollar is nothing if they add features back, but right now the radio keeps repeating songs I already know and the play counts are still hidden. Stats.fm is the only way I get any real data, so I'm staying and hoping for better.
Spotify still has no lossless tier and now they want more money. Tidal pays artists better and sounds better, so I'll keep my HiFi there and only use Spotify for Connect.

Apple Music already gives you lossless and Spatial Audio in the same plan, so Spotify going up to $10.99 with the same lossy audio is a hard sell. I keep Spotify for Connect and Android Auto but I am looking hard at switching.

Honestly the library and Discover Weekly are still why I am here, and Premium was already cheap for what you get. A few bucks more does not change much for me, though I wish the recommendations stopped repeating my own songs.
Family went up a buck, so split across the household it is still pennies per person. Annoying but it works great for us and we are not going back to ads.

Ten bucks already felt like a lot just to remove ads, and now it is eleven while the free tier keeps getting more ads. It is still good bang for the buck for the catalog, but I want to see the free tier stop getting worse at the same time.
Great, paying more for an app where the UI is a mess every other month and the recommendations are stale. If the next redesign makes it worse I am going to YouTube Music and not looking back.
Raising the price while the playlist tools still cannot handle duplicates or show liked songs is wild. Fix the sorting stuff first, then charge me more.
THEY RAISE THE PRICE AND STILL CAN'T SHOW ME MY LIKED TRACKS IN PLAYLISTS. I am seriously going back to Apple Music, I already miss adding a song to several playlists at once being easy there.
Don't care about the price, I cancelled already. I just want the renewal pop-up to stop showing up every time I open the app, clearing cache did nothing. Anyone have a fix that actually works?
Spotify raises the price and the artists still get fractions of a cent per stream. Where is the extra money going, because it is not going to the people making the music.
Cool, more money for a product that keeps taking features away. My liked songs still do not show up on album track lists, so I will unsubscribe again if that does not come back.
Price bump is annoying but nothing else matches the radio and the catalog right now. I just wish they showed exact play counts and stopped filling radio with songs I already know.
A buck more for ad-free, offline, and casting is still a steal compared with my other subscriptions combined. The free tier is still unusable so I will keep paying.
Raising the price on an app that still breaks offline downloads after every update? I have reinstalled three times and an older version is the only one that worked. Not paying more until it works.
Student plan going from $4.99 to $5.99 hurts, I'm on a tight budget. If it keeps going up I'm going back to Apple Music, even though I'll miss the Hulu bundle.
Still no lossless tier and now they want more money for it. Tidal already has hi-fi and Apple Music has lossless, so Spotify charging more while skipping the audio quality is really frustrating.
More money and shuffle still plays the same 50 songs out of my giant playlists. I pay to avoid random adds, but if I cannot get a true random shuffle I am moving to Apple Music.
I already cancelled my family plan over the podcast-stuffed home screen, so this price hike changes nothing for me. Show me the music and I would come back.
Price goes up and the home screen is still a TikTok feed with two cards on screen. This is garbage and I'm done, bring back the old UI or I'm gone for good.
Another dollar a month when I am already having a hard time paying some months. Premium is still cheap, but I will probably drop back to free until money is steadier.
Price going up while features still disappear and come back with no explanation. Still being tested, maybe, but vote with your wallet until they bring back what we had.
Spotify wants more money and still has no lossless, while Tidal pays artists better and sounds way better. I will keep Spotify for Connect and recs but the HiFi tier would be worth it, not this.
Paying more and I still hear ads in podcasts? They keep shoving podcasts down my throat too. I might just go to YouTube Premium or stick to Overcast and drop the music side.
Absolutely hate this update and now the price goes up too. If the music tab keeps the feed layout I'm switching to Apple Music, my playlists are a pain to find already.
I already cancelled and uninstalled after the last forced update, so the price does not matter to me. Keep the old version and the classic interface and I'll come back.
I'm on free so the price bump does not touch me, but I'd only pay again if the ads and random shuffle go away. Tempted but not yet.
Ten bucks for the full catalog was already an incredible deal and they should charge more given what artists get paid. Honestly a long overdue increase, and I'm still paying.
Student plan going to $5.99 stings a little, but I'm still paying it. It's still cheaper than a coffee a month. I just wish they'd finally add lossless first.
Family at $16.99 for six accounts is still absurd value. Split that many ways and it beats anything else on the market.
Honestly this is the push I needed. Apple Music is the same price now and I get lossless plus it bundles with my iCloud. Switching.
Calling it now, Rogan money is what's driving this. Ads, price hikes, whatever comes next, it's all to pay for podcasts instead of music.
Everything went up. Netflix, Disney, all of them. A dollar isn't going to break me, so I'm not going to lose sleep over it.
Can't afford it anymore. Going back to the free tier and I'll deal with the ads.
Okay, but how much of this dollar goes to artists? The per-stream payout is still garbage. If they're raising prices they should show us where it goes.
Already on YouTube Music Premium and it comes with YouTube. Done with Spotify after this hike.
Lol, I'll just go back to downloading. Not paying more for an app that keeps getting worse.
Duo going to $14.99 is annoying, but my partner and I split it and it still beats two individual plans.
Price went up a dollar. I'll get the email and roll with it.
The app has been getting worse with every update and now they want more money. The new UI is a mess and I'm not paying extra for this.
Spotify still has no lossless and now costs more. Tidal has had lossless for years. Switching.
Student at $5.99 is still the best deal in streaming. Not complaining.
I already get Amazon Music through Prime, so this doesn't touch me. Watching this one from the sidelines.
Moved our family plan down to Duo. We can't justify $16.99 for stuff we barely use, and the new price makes it worse.
Spotify posts record profits and then this. Shareholders get paid, and we get a price hike.
People need to stop acting like a dollar is the end of the world. Music costs money to license, and this is still cheap.
The ads on the free tier keep getting worse, and I'm not paying more to avoid them. I'm staying put and grumbling.
Still waiting on lossless. If they charged a dollar more for HiFi I'd pay it, but charging more for the same thing is annoying.
I've paid $9.99 since 2016 and I'm fine with this. Ad-free access to everything is still a steal.
I mostly use Spotify for audiobooks and podcasts, and that's where I'm getting hit. I'm canceling. I'll get my books from the library and skip the extra cost.
Every service is doing this. Netflix, Hulu, YouTube TV. Spotify was overdue, honestly.
Family plan is going up to $16.99 with my kids on it and I'm furious. Every price hike means we pay for six accounts more.
Honestly I'm glad they're investing in the product. I hope it means better features and a better app.
Deezer's Premium is cheaper and I've been meaning to try it for a while. This hike is what finally makes me move.
Student plan going to $5.99 stings a little, but it's still cheaper than most things I pay for. I'm staying for now.
Family plan up a dollar for six accounts is honestly fine. Still cheaper per person than anything else out there.
Paying more and still no lossless. Tidal has had HiFi for years. A price hike without the feature I actually wanted is insulting.
Spotify keeps getting pricier while Apple Music already sits at $10.99 with lossless included. Why would I stay?
Good that they say this helps artists, but I'll believe it when per-stream rates actually change. Staying for now.
Eh, a dollar. Didn't even notice until I saw the post.
I mostly pay for Premium for podcasts and audiobooks, so the bump doesn't change much for me.
I'm going back to free with ads. Not paying $11 for a playlist app that plays the same ads I'd hear anyway.
Honestly this is the push I needed. At this point I'd rather just download stuff than keep paying for it.
Duo going to $14.99 hits us hard. We'll probably drop down to individual and split things differently.
YouTube Music Premium is cheaper if you already pay for YouTube. Pretty sure I'm switching.
Stop complaining. Dozens of markets and the first US increase in over a decade is a fair ask for what you get.
Record profits and they raise prices on the people paying the bills. Classic.
The app has gotten worse with every redesign, and now I'm paying more for it. That stings.
I already pay for Prime and Amazon Music is included. Spotify just lost me with this.
Everything has gone up: streaming, groceries, rent. This was expected at this point.
Student went up a dollar, but if you're enrolled it's still the best music deal going.
I can't really afford this right now, so I'm dropping back to the free tier until things settle.
Still worth it for ad-free listening and offline downloads. A dollar more doesn't change that for me.
Our kids moved out, so we're dropping from Family to Duo. The price bump is what pushed us to finally do it.
I'd rather they put money into music and artists than into podcast deals. Every price hike seems to go to the podcast side.
Does this change the Family price for people already subscribed? The email says they'll let us know. Whatever, I'll wait.
Hope some of this actually reaches artists and not just shareholders. I'm not holding my breath.
Deezer's family plan is cheaper for our household, and it has a decent catalog. We're probably moving over.
Not sure why this is a whole post. I'm still using it and it hasn't changed my life either way.
This is the last straw. Cancelling Premium today and I'm telling everyone I know to do the same.
Student plan is now $5.99 and I'm a broke sophomore, so that's rough. Still cheaper than a Netflix sub though, so I'm staying for now.
Lol $1 more on Individual, I've been paying $9.99 since 2016. Inflation is inflation, I'll stay.
Spotify is greedy af, they had record profits last quarter and now they want more from us. Cancelled and moved to Apple Music.
